story: Campaign finance reports made public the week of July 20, 2026 show Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins with the largest reported haul in Alaska's 17-candidate governor field at 1.8 million dollars since February, including 372,000 dollars from six employees of the AI company Anthropic, while he campaigns on pausing data center construction and regulating AI, and separately says his national donors care about whether he can win rather than about policy.
source_independence_caveat: The Anchorage Daily News article and the Alaska Public Media article are the SAME article by the SAME reporter (Iris Samuels), republished. The fundraising core rests on ONE reporting source, not two. The deck must never present it as corroborated by two outlets.
conflict_of_interest: This carousel is produced by a routine running on a Claude model built by Anthropic, and six Anthropic employees are the donors at the center of the story. A visible disclosure is required on the deck and in the first comment.

claims.claim: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has brought in 1.8 million dollars since entering Alaska's governor race in February 2026.
claims.verbatim_support: Kreiss-Tomkins has brought in $1.8 million since entering the race in February.
claims.notes: Same reporter as the Alaska Public Media republication. One source, not two.

claims.claim: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is among the 17 candidates in Alaska's governor race.
claims.verbatim_support: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is among the 17 candidates in Alaska's governor race.
claims.notes: Do NOT use any party breakdown. The 12 Republicans, 2 Democrats, 1 independent figure does not sum to 17 and is rejected.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins reported the largest haul in the field, ahead of Matt Heilala at nearly 1.6 million dollars and Tom Begich at 1.1 million dollars.
claims.verbatim_support: Matt Heilala reported a total haul of nearly $1.6 million, with more than $1.4 million from himself.
claims.notes: The RANKING is DERIVED from verified per-candidate totals. Phrase as 'the largest reported haul in the field', never quote the paper as saying 'leads'.

claims.claim: Six employees of Anthropic, a California based artificial intelligence company, collectively gave Kreiss-Tomkins 372,000 dollars.
claims.verbatim_support: His top contributors include six employees of Anthropic, a California-based artificial intelligence company, who collectively gave Kreiss-Tomkins $372,000.
claims.notes: LOAD BEARING. Six individual employees. Never 'Anthropic donated' or 'Anthropic money'.

claims.claim: The campaign's largest single contribution came from an Anthropic employee named Drake Thomas, who gave 100,000 dollars.
claims.verbatim_support: Kreiss-Tomkins' largest contribution came from an Anthropic employee named Drake Thomas, who gave the campaign $100,000.

claims.claim: Drake Thomas grew up in Soldotna and now lives in Berkeley, California.
claims.verbatim_support: Kreiss-Tomkins' largest contribution came from an Anthropic employee named Drake Thomas, who grew up in Soldotna and now lives in Berkeley, California.
claims.notes: Say 'grew up in Soldotna', not 'Soldotna native'.

claims.claim: The majority of Kreiss-Tomkins's funding came from wealthy donors in the Lower 48, per Anchorage Daily News reporting.
claims.verbatim_support: The majority of Kreiss-Tomkins' funding came from wealthy donors in the Lower 48.
claims.notes: MUST be attributed to ADN. NO dollar split or percentage is verified.

claims.claim: Matt Heilala reported a total haul of nearly 1.6 million dollars, with more than 1.4 million dollars of it from himself.
claims.verbatim_support: Matt Heilala reported a total haul of nearly $1.6 million, with more than $1.4 million from himself.
claims.notes: MANDATORY COUNTER-FRAMING. One person's own checkbook exceeds the six-employee total.

claims.claim: Tom Begich reported a total haul of 1.1 million dollars.
claims.verbatim_support: Tom Begich reported a total haul of $1.1 million.
claims.notes: The 'largely Alaska money' characterization is paraphrase only. Do not name Begich donors.

claims.claim: Treg Taylor reported 1 million dollars in fundraising and Adam Crum reported raising nearly 940,000 dollars.
claims.verbatim_support: Treg Taylor reported $1 million in fundraising. Adam Crum reported raising nearly $940,000.
claims.notes: Two adjacent verbatim sentences.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins said Alaska should have a process and a policy on data centers and that until it does, nothing should happen.
claims.verbatim_support: "I think very clearly we should have a process and a policy we don't right now, and so until we do, nothing should happen," he said.
claims.notes: USE THIS EXACT WORDING if quoting.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins wants Alaska to hold AI companies liable for harms caused by their products, ban deepfakes, require the disclosure of AI in political ads, crack down on AI enabled fraud, implement protections for children against AI content, and require a human behind state decisions.
claims.verbatim_support: Kreiss-Tomkins wants Alaska to lead in adopting such regulations, including to hold AI companies liable for harms caused by their products, ban deepfakes, require the disclosure of AI in political ads, crack down on AI-enabled fraud, implement protections for children against AI content, and require a human behind state decisions.
claims.notes: The keepable list. Six items, verbatim.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins said he is a huge supporter of campaign finance reform because he does not think fundraising should have the role that it does, but that in the system we have, it is important.
claims.verbatim_support: "I'm a huge supporter of campaign finance reform because I don't think (fundraising) should have the role that it does. But in the system that we have, it's important," Kreiss-Tomkins said in an interview Thursday.
claims.notes: COUNTER-FRAMING. The parenthetical is the paper's insertion.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins said most of his national donors have only one agenda, which is whether he can win.
claims.verbatim_support: "Most of our national donors, I think, actually, their only agenda is, 'can you win?'"
claims.notes: CRITICAL COUNTER-FRAMING. Directly undercuts any causation reading. MUST APPEAR IN THE DECK.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins said that almost universally, if donors think someone can win, then national interest starts to appear.
claims.verbatim_support: "Almost universally, if donors think someone can win, then you start seeing national interest," said Kreiss-Tomkins.
claims.notes: COUNTER-FRAMING. Money follows viability.

claims.claim: Alaska's statewide primary election is August 18, 2026.
claims.verbatim_support: None of the other candidates have reported spending over $650,000 so far, leaving them with more in the bank as the Aug. 18 primary is less than a month away.
claims.notes: NOT primary-sourced. elections.alaska.gov returned 503 on three paths. Say nothing about how many candidates advance.

claims.claim: No other candidate in the race had reported spending over 650,000 dollars at the time of the filings.
claims.verbatim_support: None of the other candidates have reported spending over $650,000 so far, leaving them with more in the bank as the Aug. 18 primary is less than a month away.
claims.notes: Do not state Kreiss-Tomkins's own spending figure; it was not captured.

claims.claim: No allegation of unlawful or improper contributions is reported in this coverage.
claims.verbatim_support: "I'm a huge supporter of campaign finance reform because I don't think (fundraising) should have the role that it does. But in the system that we have, it's important," Kreiss-Tomkins said in an interview Thursday.
claims.notes: A verified ABSENCE established by reading both pages in full. Frame as 'no wrongdoing has been alleged in this reporting', NEVER as 'the donations were legal'.

claims.claim: In a June 2026 candidate survey, Kreiss-Tomkins wrote that at the end of the day it has to be people, not algorithms, making the decisions that shape our lives.
claims.verbatim_support: But at the end of the day, it has to be people — not algorithms — making the decisions that shape our lives.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, must be labeled. The verbatim contains em dashes. PARAPHRASE it on slides (house rule); do not present a dash-stripped version as a quote.

claims.claim: In the same survey Kreiss-Tomkins wrote that Alaskans' personal information belongs to Alaskans alone and should not be fed into third party systems without consent.
claims.verbatim_support: Ultimately, Alaskans' personal information belongs to Alaskans alone — it should be guarded carefully and not fed into third-party systems without consent.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Says 'personal information', not 'data'. Contains an em dash, paraphrase on slides.

claims.claim: In the same survey Kreiss-Tomkins wrote that Alaska's power and water are not a giveaway and that no Alaskan should watch their electric bill climb to subsidize a server farm.
claims.verbatim_support: Our power and water are not a giveaway. No Alaskan should watch their electric bill climb to subsidize a server farm.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Dash free, slide safe as a direct quote.

claims.claim: In the same survey Kreiss-Tomkins wrote that he worries the AI industry has downplayed the risks posed to the public and that the federal government has been totally flat footed.
claims.verbatim_support: I worry the AI industry has downplayed the risks posed to the public. The federal government has been totally flat-footed.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The sharpest verified juxtaposition in the story. Dash free.

claims.claim: Republican candidate Michael Gilbert answered the survey by saying he will not use any AI in his administration.
claims.verbatim_support: I WILL NOT use any AI in my administration.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Capitalization is the candidate's own.

claims.claim: Mat-Su borough mayor Edna DeVries ended her survey answer on AI by disclosing that she used AI to write it.
claims.verbatim_support: And of course, I used AI to answer this question.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Dash free, slide safe.

claims.claim: Republican candidate Shelley Hughes says she authored the first AI legislation in Alaska a few years ago.
claims.verbatim_support: This is why I authored the first AI legislation in Alaska a few years ago, recognizing early we must harness AI for good and safeguard against harm.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND and a CANDIDATE CLAIM ONLY. Not verified as enacted. Always 'Hughes says she authored', never 'Alaska's first AI law'.

claims.claim: Republican candidate Lesil McGuire said any algorithmic decision affecting Alaskans must have an explainable, human appealable path, and that every public facing AI output must be reviewed and signed off by a qualified state employee before release.
claims.verbatim_support: Second, any algorithmic decision affecting Alaskans (permits, benefits, eligibility, hiring) must have an explainable, human-appealable path.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. First safeguard also verified verbatim: 'First, every public-facing AI output must be reviewed and signed off by a qualified state employee before release.'

claims.claim: Independent candidate Bill Walker said manufactured ideas cannot substitute genuine, dynamic thought or input from Alaskans.
claims.verbatim_support: Manufactured ideas cannot substitute genuine, dynamic thought or input from Alaskans.

claims.verbatim_support: Republicans Bernadette Wilson, Treg Taylor and Adam Crum and independent Meda DeWitt did not respond to this edition's questions; we sent them multiple requests.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. A fifth, independent Destry Payne, was unreachable because his listed email did not work. Do NOT put a responder COUNT on a slide, the article states none.

unverified_but_reported.claim: Anthropic employee donors gave because they favor strong AI regulation.
unverified_but_reported.why: NO source states any donor's motive. Not one donor is quoted anywhere. The only on-record statement of donor motive is the candidate's, and it says the opposite. The deck MUST NOT attribute a policy motive to these donors.

unverified_but_reported.claim: Large out-of-state fundraising is unusual, or alternatively normal, in Alaska statewide races.
unverified_but_reported.why: No source characterizes the historical baseline either way. The deck cannot claim unprecedented, nor routine.

unverified_but_reported.claim: Whether Anthropic the company has any involvement.
unverified_but_reported.why: No source suggests corporate involvement. Six individual employees. Never say 'Anthropic donated'.

counter_framing_verified.point: The single largest funding source in the race is a candidate's own bank account, not AI money. Heilala put more than 1.4 million dollars of his nearly 1.6 million into his own campaign, more from one person than all six Anthropic employees combined gave.
The candidate publicly denies his national donors have a policy agenda, saying their only interest is whether he can win. This directly contradicts a causation reading.
The candidate frames national money as a structural feature of viable campaigns rather than issue capture.
The candidate is on record supporting campaign finance reform while accepting the money. Present as his stated position, not as hypocrisy the deck alleges.
A rival Democrat raised 1.1 million dollars, showing in-state fundraising at scale is achievable and the out-of-state pattern is candidate specific.
No wrongdoing is alleged anywhere in the reporting.

AI caution is not a donor-driven position in this field. A Republican goes further than Kreiss-Tomkins by refusing AI outright, and another Republican proposes appeal rights for algorithmic decisions.

honesty_notes: MUST NOT CLAIM: donor motive; that Anthropic the company gave; the 80/20 or Alaska-donor-total split; a July 17 period end; that filings went to APOC; a top-four primary rule; that Alaska has no AI statute; any status for HCR 3 or HB 259; the AIDEA Houston conveyance or the STAK lease; any donor name beyond Drake Thomas; Tao Lin; any survey responder count. MUST HEDGE: the out-of-state majority is attributed to ADN; the August 18 date rests on a news sentence, not the Division of Elections; the one-fifth share is Alaska.Ai arithmetic; 'no award announced' on the Air Force lease is an absence in the record. MUST LABEL BACKGROUND: c19 through c30. In-window is c1 through c18 plus the derived d1. FAIRNESS: c8 and c14 are mandatory on the deck. Omitting c14 would make the deck defective. The honest framing is that AI-industry money is now measurably present in this race and the candidate receiving it campaigns on AI restriction, while he himself says his national donors care about winnability rather than policy. The deck may note the juxtaposition. It may NOT assert causation.
